_doc: Point Pleasant, Main Street, as a 2D top-down map. Positions are in 32px tiles. fills paint ground rectangles [x,y,w,h] with a tile name or a list of tiles to pick from; facades are storefronts from assets/facades (pos is the bottom-left tile); props come from assets/props (pos is the bottom-centre tile); npcs, clues and doors use the case data. Interiors are small rooms the party enters through a facade door; each lists its own floor, wall colour, props, npcs and clues, and the exit is the bottom row.
name: Main Street

facades.name: Kessler Garage
facades.locked: Chained shut. A bicycle reflector hangs from the padlock.

houses.name: The Kessler house
houses.locked: Nobody answers. Somebody is watching from upstairs.

props.look: Last collection 4:30 p.m. Somebody has scratched a pair of eyes into the paint, and somebody else has tried to scratch them out.

look: The booth calls the Office. Ruth picks up on the second ring whatever the hour and asks if we've eaten.

props.look: The Mason Gas bin. Oil rags, a Register from Tuesday, and a paper cup from the diner with lipstick on it. Earl doesn't wear lipstick.

look: The Mason Gas sign. Red, tall, and it hasn't blinked since 1967. Remember that when somebody blames it.
The Office's station wagon. Three hundred thousand miles, a heater that works on Tuesdays, and Ruth's casserole dish still in the back.
props.name: The station wagon

props.look: A pickup with a church bumper sticker and a shotgun rack. The rack is empty. The ashtray is not.

look: Dark sedan. No plates. The engine's warm.
Marlene's Buick. There is a dent in the roof the size of a dinner plate, pushed in from above.

props.look: The church fence. Two metres of wire and a sign: PLEASE DO NOT FEED THE DEER. Somebody has added: OR ANYTHING ELSE.

look: Dead elm. The bark's stripped head-high all the way round.

props.look: The tallest pine on the bank. There is a rope swing in it from a summer nobody remembers.

look: The old flood stone. The 1913 mark is at my shoulder. The 1937 mark is over my head.

props.look: Kessler Garage overflow. Spark plugs, a hubcap, and a child's bicycle with no reflectors on it.
A burn barrel. Somebody has been burning newspapers. November 1966, by the one corner left.

props.name: Newspaper box
look: The Register, morning edition. 'COUNTY BUDGET PASSES.' Below the fold, smaller: 'Lights reported on Route 62 again.'
Again is doing a lot of work in that sentence.

props.look: A bench with a plaque: IN MEMORY OF THE 46. Somebody sits here every morning. The snow is worn through to the slats on one side only.

look: Cold here. Colder than the bench should be.
Coonhound. Old. Somebody's fed her this morning and she's still asking.
That's Rosie's dog. Rosie's been dead since 1980. The dog is a different dog. The name isn't.
A snowman with two red reflectors for eyes.

props.look: A kid's bicycle leaned on the lamp post. No lock, no reflectors. The reflectors have been pried off.
The last street light before Route 62. Out. The bulb is fine. Earl changed it twice.

look: A white cross at the edge of the road. No name. Fresh plastic flowers, this week's.
It isn't for a car accident.

props.look: A library bin. Overdue notices, torn in half. One is addressed to A. Weller, December 1967. Twenty-six years of postage due.

look: A rental, Ohio plates, parked crooked in front of the Lowe. Somebody checked in with a bad feeling and a rush.

props.look: A county truck with a plough blade and a bumper sticker: I BRAKE FOR NOTHING. The plough has not been used. The snow has.

look: A bench facing the hotel. Somebody has carved a circle with a line through it into the arm. Old, and not idle.

props.look: The hotel's planter. Dead geraniums under snow and one lit cigarette, just set down.

props.name: Courthouse bulletin board
look: COUNTY NOTICES. Pinned over the top in a fresh hand: 'Whoever's buying up all the red bicycle reflectors at Harmon's, the Sheriff knows.' Under it, smaller: 'Bobby K. doesn't.'
Today's rumour. Tomorrow's will be worse.

props.look: The courthouse bench. Three cigarette butts and a tin of Skoal, ground into the snow with care.

look: A snowman in a deputy's hat. The hat is real.
The deputy is going to want that back.
Beagle. Belongs to the courthouse, the way a cat belongs to a barn.
He won't go near the board.

props.look: Stacked lumber behind the garage, and a tarp over something the shape of a board with two holes in it.

clues.name: Something on the fence
clues.text: A tuft of grey fur caught on the top wire of the church fence. The wire is two metres up.

clues.name: A ring in the snow
clues.text: Behind the church the snow has melted in a ring two metres across. The grass under it is black. The air inside the ring feels wrong.

clues.name: Glow in the ditch
clues.text: The ditch behind Mason Gas is glowing. Faintly, blue-green, under a skin of ice.

clues.name: Something in the snow
clues.text: A roll of 35mm film, half buried behind the motel. The canister is open. Whoever dropped it was running.

clues.name: Tracks by the Kessler house
clues.text: Three-toed tracks in the snow leading to the back door. Look closer: under each claw mark, pressed flat, the tread of a boot.

clues.name: Prints in the frozen mud
clues.text: Where Main Street gives out toward the river, the mud is frozen hard and holds three-toed prints a foot long. A grey feather lies beside them.

props.look: A walk-in's worth of pie filling and one shelf of Sunday hams. Taped inside the door: a 1966 price list, kept for the day they bring prices back.

look: Everything drips in threes if you listen long enough.

props.look: The punch clock. Marlene's card has two punches a day, 5 a.m. and 9 p.m., and no punch out between them for twenty years.

look: Bunn-O-Matic. The left pot has been on since morning and tastes like the bottom of the river.
Coconut cream. Teddy has already decided.

props.name: Corkboard
props.look: The corkboard. A lost-cat flyer from 1991, still hopeful. A casserole sign-up for the bridge memorial. A fresh card in blue ballpoint: 'LIGHTS OVER THE WATER TOWER TUESDAY. NOT KIDS.' No name.
The eighth stool. Nobody sits on it. The regulars say it's Dwight Mason's and Dwight Mason hasn't been in since Tuesday.
Red vinyl, split and taped. Under the table, in marker: BOBBY K WAS HERE 1992. Under that, in a neater hand: SO WAS I.

look: The corner booth. Four coffee rings on the table in a square, every morning, same four places.

props.look: A feed-store calendar. February 1994. Marlene has circled the 15th and written 'again' in it.

clues.name: The kitchen bin
clues.text: The kitchen bin. Grease, grounds, and under the liner where it has been for a very long time, a Rosie's check dated 11/17/66: four coffees. A phone number in pencil on the back, 675-2211. The cook is watching you.

clues.name: The morning's rumour card
clues.text: An index card pinned to the corkboard. Blue ballpoint, block capitals: 'LIGHTS OVER THE WATER TOWER TUESDAY. NOT KIDS.' Pinned this morning; the hole is fresh.

look: An Underwood. The 'o' sticks. Every front page since 1952 has had slightly square zeroes.

props.look: A sheriff's calendar from the tyre place. February 1994. Every Tuesday has a pencil tick and no note.

props.name: Case board
props.look: The motel's rates card, and under it our case board. Ruth has pinned a postcard to the corner so it looks like a vacation.

clues.name: Room 14 window
clues.locked_text: The door to room 14 is locked. The clerk has the key.
clues.text: Room 14, second floor, no balcony. Three long scratches on the outside of the glass, at head height, as if something hung there.

props.name: Noticeboard
props.look: The parish noticeboard. FOOD PANTRY TUESDAYS. BRIDGE MEMORIAL, DEC 15, 26 YEARS. A casserole sign-up with Marlene down for two and the deputy down for 'rolls (store)'.
The stair down to the basement pantry. The light switch is at the bottom. The pastor says that's a test of faith and the deacons say it's a code violation.
Pantry stock, labelled by a parish hand: GREEN BEANS 1993, PEACHES 1993, PEACHES 1966. The 1966 peaches are on top.

props.name: Pantry ledger
look: The pantry sign-out ledger, 1965 to now. December 1967: a page torn out. January 1968: 'A. W., 2 cans soup, no address.' In the pastor's hand: 'Paid.'
She was still here in January.

props.look: Lost and found. One mitten, one hymnal, one pair of men's black sunglasses, folded, new.

clues.name: Cans on the pantry floor
clues.text: Three cans of peaches knocked off the bottom shelf, dented, each one punched clean through by something with three points. Grey hair in the punctures.

look: A photo of Walt and a woman on the old bridge, 1965. She's laughing. He has written on the back: BEFORE.

props.look: The station phone. Earl has written one number on the wall above it in grease pencil and crossed it out four times. It's the same number each time.

props.name: Map rack
look: Road maps, West Virginia and Ohio, 1993. One is missing from the rack and the man in the suit has it.
Penrose got there first. He's going to keep getting there first until we stop following.

props.look: A Snap-on calendar. Still on December. Not December 1993.
Coke machine. Takes dimes. Somebody has jammed a 1966 dime in the slot and the machine has been thinking about it ever since.
Oil rags and a pair of black gloves, new, the price tag still on. Harmon's Variety, $4.99.

clues.name: A map left open on the counter
clues.text: A road map, folded open to the north of the county. The TNT area is circled in pencil. North of it, where the old power plant stands, a small neat tick, and the letters W.P.

props.look: The camping aisle. Film, batteries, flashlights, Sterno, and a sign: NO RETURNS ON FLASHLIGHTS AFTER DARK.

look: Plaster, salt, sample bags. Harmon stocks for us like he's been expecting us.

props.look: Dry goods, and one shelf of 'souvenirs': a postcard of the old bridge, a jar of bolts from it, a glass eye. The eye is not for sale.
Kodak Gold, 24 exposures. Harmon keeps it cold.
D cells by the box.
Sandwich bags, sold to hunters as 'evidence bags' at twice the price.

look: Rock salt, for the walk. It will serve.

props.look: A thermos and paper cups. Honour box, fifty cents. The box has a dollar in it and an IOU from the deputy.

props.name: Behind the counter
look: Behind the counter: a crate marked HARDWARE, DAY 2 STOCK. Bolt cutters on top, still tagged.
Harmon says the truck comes Thursday. The truck is right there.

props.look: Patent medicines and Mason jars. One jar is labelled TNT AREA WATER, DO NOT DRINK, $2. It glows a little.
A rack of postcards. 'Greetings from Point Pleasant, W. Va.' The bridge on the front is the old one.
Casting plaster. Harmon sells more of it in winter than any town this size should.

look: Harmon's tree. Lights still up, still on. The angel on top has had her face turned to the wall.

props.name: Key rack
look: Key pigeonholes, four rows. The fourth row has one hook and it is turned to the wall.
A hotel with a floor it won't rent. That's a story or it's plumbing.

props.name: The register
props.look: The guest register, open to this week. Three names. One is a Columbus salesman who has written 'NO' in the box for 'How did you hear of us?'
A lobby clock, stopped at 5:04. The Silver Bridge fell at 5:04 p.m. Nobody has wound it since and nobody is going to.

look: The Lowe in 1901, when it was new and the river was the way in. The paddleboat in the picture burned in 1911.

props.look: A lobby sofa. Somebody slept on it last night. Somebody with very long legs and no shoes.
A loveseat under the window. The cushion on the left is worn through; the one on the right has never been sat on.
A basket of matchbooks. THE LOWE HOTEL, POINT PLEASANT, ON THE OHIO. Take one.
The back stairs, roped off. The rope is velvet and the dust on it is twenty-six years deep.

clues.name: Room 412
clues.text: Up four flights, the room she rented. The bed is made. On the desk by the window, one case card in a tall slanting hand: POINT PLEASANT, DEC 1967. A. WELLER. Every line filled but the verdict, and under the verdict line, pressed hard enough to tear: NOT HOAX. W.P. WAS HERE FIRST.

props.look: Fiction, A to L. Every Louis L'Amour is out. The night clerk at the Lowe has them.

look: Local history. The Mason County centennial book, 1904. The chapter on the Shawnee is three pages and apologises for two of them.

props.look: The returns pile. A county plat book is on the overdue list in red, borrowed December 12th, 1967. The borrower's card is still active.

props.name: Local studies
props.look: LOCAL STUDIES. Microfiche of the Register, 1950 to 1990, by year. 1967 is filed in front of 1966. Somebody has had it out recently.
Vertical files. CLIPPINGS, BRIDGE. CLIPPINGS, FLOOD. CLIPPINGS, MISC. The MISC folder is the fattest and it is empty.

clues.name: Microfiche reader
clues.locked_text: The reader is dark. The local studies fiche is behind the desk and Dot pulls it by request only.
clues.text: The Register on fiche, November 1966 to December 1967. Page after page of lights, birds and letters. Then December 18th, 1967, three days after the bridge: a two-inch notice. 'Federal investigators conclude Route 62 sightings a hoax. W. Penrose, Office of Special Inquiry.' There is no such office.

props.look: Guns and tools, tagged by month. Three deer rifles, two chainsaws, and a box of wrenches from a garage that closed in December. Nobody comes back for wrenches in February.

look: Radios, a Polaroid, a wedding band in a coffee cup. Every town's got a shelf like this. This one's fuller.
River's been up twice this winter. Folks hock what's dry.
Church silver. A communion plate, a candlestick, a crucifix with the figure pried off.
Somebody needed the silver more than the figure.

props.look: A feed store calendar, still on November. Somebody has circled the 15th and written WAIT.
A grandfather clock, stopped at twenty to midnight. The tag says NOT FOR SALE and under that, smaller, NOT A CLOCK.

look: A Hallicrafters, pawned Tuesday. Somebody retuned it before they let it go. It's parked on nothing. Dead air.
You don't tune a radio to dead air by accident.

props.name: Glass case
look: The glass case. Rings, watches, a Purple Heart, a Silver Bridge token on a chain and a 1966 class ring, Point Pleasant High, initials D.M.
Dwight Mason's ring. In a pawn shop. Four days after he stopped coming to the diner.

props.look: The ledger. Every ticket for four months. Tuesday's page has been torn out and taped back in, and one line is written harder than the rest.

look: A camera bag with no camera in it. Pawned, the tag says, by a 'reporter, Columbus'. There's still film in the side pocket.
Nobody from Columbus is covering this.
A kid's bike, pawned for four dollars. Reflectors gone. Not pried. Unscrewed, careful, like somebody meant to put them back.

props.look: A crate marked RIVER, chalked $5 THE LOT. Waders, a bilge pump, a car battery, and a life jacket from the towboat line with the name cut out.

look: A hand mirror hung as a wall mirror. The glass is older than the frame.

encounters.intro: A man in a dark suit is standing where there was nobody a second ago. He knows your name.
encounters.win: He walks away without turning around. The street is the street again.
